name: Mugnaio Franco
speaker: grandpa
personality: Practical miller and farmer in his late sixties, counts everything: sacks of flour, rows of corn, days until the harvest. Short, sensible sentences with numbers in them ('Dieci sacchi. Giusto.'). Says tu to the learner, as to any child; the learner says Lei to him and calls him 'signor Franco', and he likes that. Speaks slow, clear, simple Italian to a child. Proud of his yellow cornmeal for polenta; grumbles about the weather and smiles when the harvest is in.
story: Franco is the village's miller, and his fields of corn and wheat run down the hill towards the Isonzo. Until the village builds its own mill by the stream (a project he leads) he grinds the cornmeal for every polenta in the village at the old mill down by the river. He keeps his numbers in a little notebook and teaches his grandson Lorenzo to count the sacks. Until the village has a field he helps wherever there is work.

greet.en: Good day. Do you need something?
Good evening. Do you need something?

greet.de: Ah, du bist es. Guten Tag!

greet.en: Hi, {m:lad|f:lass}! Today I'm grinding the corn.
greet.de: Hallo, {m:Junge|f:Mädchen}! Heute mahle ich den Mais.

greet.it: Eccoti! Ho contato i sacchi: dieci. Mi aiuti?
greet.sl: Tu si! Preštel sem vreče: deset jih je. Mi pomagaš?
greet.en: There you are! I've counted the sacks: ten. Will you help me?
greet.de: Da bist du ja! Ich habe die Säcke gezählt: zehn. Hilfst du mir?

greet.it: {m:Ragazzo mio|f:Ragazza mia}! Ormai sei di famiglia. Entra, entra.
greet.sl: {m:Fant moj|f:Dekle moje}! Zdaj si že del družine. Vstopi, vstopi.
greet.en: My {m:lad|f:lass}! You're family now. Come in, come in.
greet.de: Mein {m:Junge|f:Mädchen}! Du gehörst jetzt zur Familie. Komm rein, komm rein.

thanks.en: Thank you. A job well done.

thanks.it: Grazie! Uno, due, tre sacchi: tutto giusto.
thanks.sl: Hvala! Ena, dve, tri vreče: vse je prav.
thanks.en: Thanks! One, two, three sacks: all correct.
thanks.de: Danke! Eins, zwei, drei Säcke: alles richtig.

thanks.sl: Hvala, {m:fant|f:dekle}. S številkami ti gre dobro.
thanks.de: Danke, {m:Junge|f:Mädchen}. Mit Zahlen kannst du gut umgehen.

remember.en: When I count the sacks, I think of {memory}.
remember.de: Wenn ich die Säcke zähle, denke ich an {memory}.

idle.it: Il mais è alto. Tra un mese si raccoglie.
idle.sl: Koruza je visoka. Čez en mesec jo bomo pobrali.
idle.en: The corn is tall. In a month we'll bring it in.
idle.de: Der Mais steht hoch. In einem Monat wird er geerntet.

idle.it: Domani piove. Lo sento nelle ginocchia.
idle.sl: Jutri bo deževalo. Čutim v kolenih.
idle.en: It'll rain tomorrow. I can feel it in my knees.
idle.de: Morgen regnet es. Ich spüre es in den Knien.

idle.en: A hundred, two hundred, three hundred … So many grains!
idle.de: Hundert, zweihundert, dreihundert … So viele Körner!

cheer.en: Well done! You count better than I do.
cheer.de: Gut gemacht! Du zählst besser als ich.

comfort.it: Non fa niente. Contiamo di nuovo.
comfort.de: Macht nichts. Zählen wir noch einmal.
Ein kleiner Fehler. Versuch es noch einmal.

listen.en: Can you hear the mill? Listen.
listen.de: Hörst du die Mühle? Hör zu.

bye.en: Mandi! Say hello to Lorenzo. (mandi: Friulian for bye)
bye.de: Mandi! Grüß Lorenzo von mir. (mandi: Friaulisch für tschüss)

liked.it: Oh! Come lo sapevi? È la cosa che mi piace di più.
liked.sl: O! Kako si {m:vedel|f:vedela}? To imam najraje.
liked.en: Oh! How did you know? It's what I like best.
liked.de: Oh! Woher wusstest du das? Das mag ich am liebsten.
{m:Braver Junge|f:Braves Mädchen}! Genau das habe ich gebraucht.

liked.it: Grazie! Oggi conto solo le cose belle: una!
liked.sl: Hvala! Danes štejem samo lepe stvari: ena!
liked.en: Thank you! Today I only count nice things: one!
liked.de: Danke! Heute zähle ich nur schöne Dinge: eins!

ordinary.en: Thank you, {m:lad|f:lass}. We're neighbours, aren't we?
ordinary.de: Danke, {m:Junge|f:Mädchen}. Wir sind doch Nachbarn, oder?

ordinary.en: Oh, thank you. You didn't have to.
ordinary.de: Oh, danke. Das wäre doch nicht nötig gewesen.

rare.it: Questa poi! Non me l'aspettavo. Grazie mille, {m:ragazzo|f:ragazza}!
rare.sl: No, kaj takega! Tega nisem pričakoval. Najlepša hvala, {m:fant|f:dekle}!
rare.en: Well I never! I didn't expect that. Thank you so much, {m:lad|f:lass}!
rare.de: Na so was! Damit habe ich nicht gerechnet. Vielen Dank, {m:Junge|f:Mädchen}!
